### Designs in team workspaces stay in the team workspace
Designs created inside a Canva Teams workspace belong to that workspace. If you cancel your Canva Teams plan or remove members, they’ll lose access to designs created in that team.
Download or share important designs before making changes. Your personal designs (created outside the team workspace) are always accessible from your account.

If your Canva Teams subscription lapses or is canceled, your designs stay saved and accessible; they’re not deleted.

# Add and apply color themes
Apply coordinated colors to your design in one click using color themes. Themes update your background, elements, and text together to keep your designs consistent.
Color themes are different from brand colors. Brand colors are a palette, while themes define how those colors are applied across your design.
**Check if you can use color themes:**
- Available to Canva Pro, Canva Teams, Canva Business, Canva Enterprise, Canva Education, and Canva for Nonprofits users with Brand Kit access.
- Creating and editing color themes requires Brand Kit edit access. In team Brand Kits, only owners, admins, and brand designers can manage themes.
- If you have edit access, you can create themes from suggestions or by extracting them from a design. Creating themes from scratch isn’t available.

Color themes automatically update supported elements in your design.
**Themes work with:**
- Backgrounds (including gradients)
- Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG)
- Text
**Themes don't apply to:**
- PNG or JPG images
- Charts
- Locked elements
- Gradients on elements or text (these are replaced with solid colors)

To maximize your website’s functionality, you can integrate your Canva domain with other third-party services by changing the DNS records. Here’s how.

### Why would I need to edit my DNS records?

For example, if you initially marked option A as correct and received submissions for option B, those would be marked as incorrect. ## What are the limitations of Polls and Quizzes?
- You can add up to**10 questions per form**.

# Audio protected by third-party copyright
We know it’s frustrating when you can’t download your design. This may happen if your design contains copyrighted audio.
Canva uses audio fingerprinting to detect music that matches copyrighted content. It works like a digital tool that recognizes songs, similar to apps that identify music playing nearby. When a match is found, Canva may block the download to protect copyright holders.
## Why audio gets blocked
Canva may block your download if:
- The audio matches content registered by a copyright holder.
- The audio was uploaded without the right permissions.
- The audio comes from a provider whose license doesn’t allow use in videos.
Tip: Audio from Canva’s library marked **Commercial use allowed** is designed for use in published content.

Yes, you can. However, when copying 3D styles to elements, the result can’t be rotated as they remain technically 2D graphics with 3D styling.

Yes. Select a graphic, copy its art style, then select a photo to apply the style. The photo will change to match the graphic's look.

No. You can only copy art styles from graphics. You can apply styles to photos, but you can't use a photo as the source.

Style Match uses AI to change how your photo looks. When you apply styles to photos of people, facial features or skin tones may look different. Try a different style or report the content if results are unexpected.

# Create a clear design preview thumbnail
The **preview thumbnail** is the small image that represents your design on the homepage and in folders. It helps you and your team quickly spot the right file without opening each one.
## **How thumbnails are generated**
The first page of your design is used as the thumbnail for all design types, including:
- Presentations and Documents
- Whiteboards and Webpages
- Templates and Social posts
If the first page is blank, filled with white elements on a white background, or overly cluttered, the thumbnail may be hard to recognize in shared team spaces.
## **Options for controlling your thumbnail**
You can choose one of two ways to make your design easier to recognize.
### **Option 1: Content-based thumbnail**
If your design starts with a meaningful page, like a title slide, report cover, or social media post, that’ll be set as the thumbnail automatically. This works best for standalone des

### **Option 2: Dedicated preview page**
For more complex documents or team templates, you can add a dedicated first page just for the thumbnail. This helps create a consistent look across your organization.
**To set a dedicated thumbnail page:**
1. Open your design and select **Add page**.
2. Select **Move up** or drag the page to the top so it becomes **Page 1**.
3. Design this page with high-contrast text and brand elements.
4. Include the **design type** (e.g., "Monthly Report" or "Social Media Kit") so users know what to expect before opening the file.

Clear thumbnails help your team find the right file faster and avoid misclicks, especially when working with lots of designs.
- **Keep it simple:** Thumbnails are small, so use large, readable fonts and avoid overcrowding the page with fine details.
- **Apply Brand Kits:** Use your **Brand Kit** colors and fonts for a consistent look across team folders.
- **Use visual cues:** Color-code or label thumbnails by department (e.g., blue for Marketing, green for HR) to make them easier to scan.
- **Label template versions:** If multiple versions exist, include the version or region on the thumbnail (e.g., "Q4 Sales Presentation – EMEA").

### **Do personal Brand Kits have the same features as other Brand Kits?**
Personal Brand Kits support many of the same features, with a few differences:
- Each person can create one personal Brand Kit per user.
- Personal Brand Kits don’t include a guidelines document. Use category guidelines and dos and don’ts instead.
- You can’t create personal Brand Kits in folders or add them to folders, and categories don’t support linking to folders.
### **Can a personal Brand Kit be shared for others to edit?**
No. It’s shared for view and use access only. This applies even if it’s shared with an admin or brand designer.
### **Who can see a personal Brand Kit?**
Personal Brand Kits are private to the person who creates them. Admins and brand designers can’t view or edit them. For Enterprise customers, activity is included in audit logs so admins can maintain team oversight.

Canva Video has transformed from a page-based tool to a full video editor that gives you more flexibility and control at your fingertips:

- **Direct clip editing**: Trim, split, and arrange clips from the timeline

## Understanding the video timeline
### What is the timeline?
The timeline is your video editing workspace at the bottom of the editor. It shows your clips, audio, and elements laid out over time. It’s a visual map of your video, showing what plays when and how everything is layered.
### Key components
- **Playhead**: A vertical line that shows your current position. Drag it to move through your video.
- **Time ruler**: Displays time in seconds and minutes along the top of the timeline.
- **Track area**: The space where you place and arrange video clips, audio, and elements.
- **Play controls**: Lets you play, pause, and preview your video during editing.
- **Plus button:**Where you can add videos, photos, and backgrounds
- **Add Audio button**: Use this to browse and add music or

### How do tracks work?
Tracks help organize your video so each part plays at the right time and in the right order.
- **Main track**: This is the thick track in the timeline with the plus button beside it. Use this for your main videos, photos or background clips. Clips in this track play one after another with no gaps.
- **Upper track**: Use this for text, graphics, or other visuals that appear on top of your video. You can also drag anything from the main track into upper tracks to layer your media on the timeline (overlays). Clips here can overlap and play at the same time.
- **Audio tracks**: This is a separate section for music, sound effects, and voiceovers.

# Create multiple designs faster with Bulk Create and Data Autofill
Need to make lots of designs from existing data? Canva’s **Bulk Create** and **Data Autofill** features can help you do just that—quickly and efficiently.
Here’s how they work and when to use each one:
## Bulk Create: Turn spreadsheets into designs
Use Bulk Create to generate multiple designs at once. You can import data from a spreadsheet or a supported data app, and Canva will automatically fill in the text and images for each design.
Best for:
Creating ready-to-share designs, like social posts, name tags, or ads.

# Create one Canva project with multiple design types
## What is a multi-design in Canva?
Create and manage several designs (like social posts, flyers, and presentations) all in one Canva project. A multi-design project is perfect for campaigns or events that need different formats with consistent branding.
## Create a multi-design project
Creating a multi-design or adding a new page type is available to all users.
### Create a multi-design
1. Next to the last page of your design, click **Add page type**.**Note**: The**Add page**button adds a same-size page, while the **Add page type** dropdown opens the multi-design (page type options) feature.
2. Select your preferred option.
Your design will now include a new page with the selected page type.

# Credit or debit card errors
## Why did I get a credit or debit card error?
### What can cause this
- Your card may not have enough funds.
- You're using an unsupported card.
- You entered incorrect card details.
- Your card might not be activated or enabled for international and online purchases.
- Your bank incorrectly marked your payment to Canva as fraudulent.
- You're making an unauthorized purchase.
### What to do
- Check if your card has enough funds.
- Use a Visa, Mastercard, American Express, Discover, JCB, or Diners card.
- Double-check your card details (card number, expiry date, and CVV code).
- If you’re a team owner or team admin entering the card details through a download or upgrade prompt, try adding it from **Billing** in **Settings**.
- If you’re paying from the mobile app, check the card linked to your App Store or Play Store account. You can also reach out to Apple or Google Support for help.
-

### Contacting your bank
If you’ve checked your card details and you have enough funds, it's best to contact your bank. Your bank should be able to provide more details on why they declined the payment.
You can contact your bank by calling the number on your card or through online/mobile banking. Make sure to provide them with the exact date and time of the payment, the currency and amount, and ask why this specific payment to Canva was declined.

# Design with print colors
Ever wonder why colors on screens sometimes look different than when they’re printed? That's because screens and printers use different color models. This results in a different range of colors per model.
To help match the screen and printed colors, you can use CMYK colors while designing. You can also download a CMYK file after.
## Understanding color models
RGB and CMYK are color models used to build colors. Let’s understand how color models affect the designing and printing experience.
RGB is an additive color model created by mixing red, green, and blue light together, used for digital displays like monitors and phones. Because it’s light-based, RGB can produce bright, saturated, or neon-like colors on your screen.
On the other hand, CMYK is a subtractive color model optimized for paper and physical materials. Colors are built by layering cyan, magenta, yellow, and black inks for pri

meta.title: Design with print colors
meta.text:
# Design with print colors
YK is a subtractive color model optimized for paper and physical materials. Colors are built by layering cyan, magenta, yellow, and black inks for printing. Since inks absorb and reflects light, the color range is naturally more limited.
## Converting RGB to CMYK
When your design is sent for printing, the colors are automatically converted from RGB values to the closest possible CMYK match.
The conversion works well for most colors. But ultra-bright RGB colors such as electric blues or hot pinks fall “out of gamut”. This means that they can’t be replicated exactly in print, and you might notice these colors appear softer or more muted.
If you’re planning to print your design, we recommend designing with CMYK-safe colors from the start. Designing with the output in mind helps align the colors of your design when printed.
Our support team doesn’t review designs before printing. We recommen

Our support team doesn’t review designs before printing. We recommend you [proof your designs](https://www.canva.com/help/proof-designs-print/) carefully, and select print-friendly (CMYK) colors.
## Best practices when designing for print
While slight color variations sometimes happen, there are simple ways to help you create designs that look accurate both on screen and in your hands.
### Choose print-safe colors
While super bright or highly saturated colors (like neon pinks or vivid purples) look great on screen, they may appear more muted or washed out when printed. Choosing slightly lighter versions of these types of colors can help get closer to your intended look. Scroll down to **the Using** **CMYK colors in Canva** section, or refer to the image below for the recommended colors.

### Understand how different materials affect print colors
Your choice of material can influence how colors appear on your final prints. Here's what to expect:
- **Gloss and matte finishes** on paper products will show very similar color accuracy, with gloss having a shinier surface reflection and matte offering a more subtle appearance. Both translate your screen colors quite well.
- **Uncoated and specialty papers** (like hemp) may show softer, warm color tones compared to coated options, though the difference is usually minimal.
- **Non-paper products** like mugs, mouse pads, tote bags, and apparel use different printing methods and materials, which can affect how colors appear compared to your screen. We recommend using the print preview and ordering one p

### Order one copy as test print, if possible
Nearly every product allows you to order a single copy, making it affordable to test your design before committing to larger quantities. Try experimenting with how the colors will look on different paper finishes and make any tweaks before your big order. Learn more about [ordering prints](https://www.canva.com/help/order-prints/).

**Viewer compatibility**: The protected PDF must be opened in a standard PDF reader that supports password-protected files.
**Alternative access control**: For more flexible sharing and access control, consider using Canva’s secure or private link sharing instead of password-protected downloads.

# Dynamic guides in Canva Print
Dynamic print guidelines or dynamic guides simulate where the trimming, folding, or binding area on print products. These are activated on a design when the print order panel is open.
The guidelines help visualize the final product and adjust elements to ensure that any important elements won’t be trimmed off or obscured by binding before placing an order.
Dynamic guides are available for the following printable design types or products:
- Trifold brochures
- Bound Document
- Notebook
- Wall Calendar
### Use dynamic guides in Canva Print
1. Click on the **Print with Canva** button.
2. Ensure that the design has **enough pages**: Wall calendar: 26 pages
3. Bound document: 10 pages (minimum)
4. Check and adjust each page to ensure that important elements don't overlap the trimming or binding area.
5. Click the **Download PDF**to make it easier to review what your design will look like when

### Tips on using dynamic guides
- Zoom in while in the editor to see how well your design elements align with the guides.

7. Paste the embed code or link onto your website.
For platforms that don’t support HTML embed codes, we suggest using smart embed links. They work on many websites, including the following:
- WordPress.com
- Medium
- Any website with oEmbed support

# Fix offline editing errors and sync issues
If you're having trouble with offline editing, learn how to fix sync issues, recover changes, and avoid common problems.
## What you need to know
- Your changes are **saved locally on your device** while offline.
- You must reconnect within **7 days** to sync your changes.
- Keep Canva open and stay online until you see **All changes synced.**
- Avoid clearing browser data or signing out while offline.
Avoid adding video or audio while offline, as this can cause broken media or prevent your changes from saving when you reconnect.
Looking for something specific?

- **Ready for offline use** - You can edit with

Create original background music without leaving your design. Generate music, sound effects, and voiceovers in the Canva editor using AI.

## Copyright and content rules
You can’t use Canva AI audio generation to:
- Copy or recreate copyrighted songs
- Generate audio “in the style of” a specific artist if it’s intended to imitate them
- Use prompts that request protected brand music or well-known soundtracks
If your request is blocked, try rewriting your prompt to describe mood, genre, instruments, and tempo instead. Learn more about [AI music generation: usage and languages](https://www.canva.com/help/ai-music-generation-usage-and-languages/).

### I can’t see AI music generation
If you don’t see the option to generate music, don’t worry, here are a few possible reasons:
- The feature may still be rolling out to your account.
- Your current plan may not include access yet.
### My prompt was rejected
If your music request didn’t go through, here are some common reasons:
- It may have referenced a specific song, artist, or recognizable track.
- It may have included copyrighted or protected material.
- It may have included violent or inappropriate themes.
To fix it, try:
- Removing artist names, song titles, or brand references.
- Describing the style instead (for example: mood, genre, instruments, tempo).

Providing additional context around the text can help the machine translation interpret the text more accurately.

Incorrect punctuation can be misinterpreted by the machine translation, resulting in translation errors.
### Break down long sentences
Long sentences can be difficult for machine translation to interpret. Break them down into shorter, simpler sentences.

This article is for Canva users in Brazil who pay for a yearly plan in 12X monthly installments using a local credit card.

### When you choose a yearly plan with installments:
- Your bank pays Canva the full yearly fee upfront.

- Your bank splits this into 12 monthly payments, which you repay directly to them.
- You don’t pay Canva directly. The installments are between you and your bank.
If your statement shows the full yearly charge, this reflects your bank reserving the credit limit. You’ll still see monthly installment charges appear separately. If you don’t see the first installment charge within three days, contact Canva support to confirm you’re enrolled.

# I can’t edit my photo, WebGL isn’t enabled
WebGL is a technology that helps run the Canva photo editor. You can have photo editing issues if WebGL isn’t enabled or supported by your browser or device.
For a smooth photo editing experience, check if your browser or device supports WebGL and make sure to enable it.
## Check if your browser supports WebGL
To check if your browser supports WebGL, visit this [WebGL checker page](https://get.webgl.org/). A spinning cube means that WebGL is enabled and working properly on your browser.
If your browser doesn’t support WebGL, see the sections below on how to enable it.
## Enable WebGL on your browser
Many browsers already support WebGL. If WebGL is supported but isn’t working properly, try updating your browser to its latest version.
If you’re using your browser’s latest version and WebGL is still not working, learn how to enable it manually from your browser’s settings.

Keeping your designs organized helps your team work faster, stay consistent, and easily find the content they need. Canva provides tools that help you organize your files, manage shared content, and keep your workspace tidy as your team grows.
## 1. Use folders to group related designs
Folders help you structure your designs by department, project, campaign, or content type.
Learn how to [create folders](https://www.canva.com/help/create-folders/).

- Use consistent naming across your team.
- Create subfolders for complex projects.

Locking an element or page in your design prevents it from being moved, resized, or edited. This helps you avoid making unintentional changes while you edit other parts of your design.

## Deploy the Canva Desktop App to an organization using an MSIX package
Canva provides a Microsoft App Package (MSIX) installer for the Canva Desktop App. The MSIX installer allows for centralized management and distribution of the Canva Desktop App across an organization's devices. Using standard Windows application management tools, IT admins can deploy and update the Canva Desktop App at scale, ensuring that employees have access to the latest design features while maintaining compliance with organizational policies, such as security updates.
The MSIX packaging format supports installation on operating systems running Windows 10 and later. It can be delivered to client devices using standard device and application management tools (for example, Microsoft Intune and Microsoft Endpoint Configuration Manager), PowerShell cmdlets, or AppInstaller. Most pending states are caused by **DNS (Domain Name System**) still propagating, conflicting A records, or host formatting rules. Use the steps below to identify and fix the issue.
## **Identify the causes of a pending DNS status**
DNS records may stay pending for a few common reasons:
- The record wasn’t added in the format your **domain provider** expects.
- Another DNS record is causing a conflict.
- DNS changes need time to spread across the internet. The update may not be finished yet.
Below are the clearest steps you can take for a quick fix.
### **Step 1: Check for conflicting or duplicate A records**
If your Canva A record has the same name/host as another existing A record, the domain host won’t know which one to use.
### **How to fix it:**

2. Look for **other A records** with the **same name/host**
3. **Remove** or **up

# Premium elements
We have an extensive library of high-quality free images, videos, audio, and other graphics. For a wider range of choices, you can also purchase premium elements.
Premium elements will have watermarks (criss-cross patterns) on your design until they’re purchased.
To remove the watermarks, you can purchase premium elements using these options:

# Proof your designs for print
Ready to print your design? Don’t forget to proof and check your design to make sure it’s ready to be printed.
Here are the things you can do when proofing.
For Canva Print orders, we may not be able to check your design for quality control before it goes to print, so make sure you [use CMYK colors](https://www.canva.com/help/cmyk-for-print/) and proof your designs before placing your order.
## Automated proofing
Canva automatically detects issues in your design to ensure that it’ll print accurately.
Detected issues are presented per page so you can review them each. **Switch a toggle on to fix** a detected issue and **switch it off to undo**.
Toggle on **fix all issues** to apply all recommended fixes. The changes will automatically reflect on your design.
If you’d like to fix an issue manually, click **Learn more**. You’ll be prompted to a brief description of the issue and details on

If you’d like to fix an issue manually, click **Learn more**. You’ll be prompted to a brief description of the issue and details on how to fix them.
Note that we’re still improving this feature and we might not be able to detect other possible issues. Hence, we recommend that you still check on the suggestions below.
## Manual proofing
### Check the font size
Just because it looks big on screen doesn’t mean it’ll be as readable when printed. Different print products have different recommended font sizes. We generally recommend not going lower than font size 7.
Canva’s automated proofing flags texts that are below the recommended minimum font size. To fix, simply go to the flagged text and increase the font size.
Viewing your design at 100% zoom will also give you an idea of how small or big the font size is.
The best way to check how your text will look is to do a test

Double-check your text content for correct spelling, grammar, and other details (e.g. dates, names, location, etc.). And don’t forget to check all e-mail addresses and social media handles.

# Request design access
When you click on a link to a Canva design that’s **not shared to you**, you won’t be able to see it. To fix this, you can request for access from its owner:
1. Log in to your Canva account, and click the **design link** to open it.
2. Click on the **Request Access** button to notify its owner of your request.
3. After the design owner [grants you access](https://www.canva.com/help/share-permissions/), you’ll be notified via email. Open that email, and click on **Open design**. You should be able to access it now.

This usually happens when you’re part of multiple teams, and a design is [shared to everyone in a team](https://www.canva.com/help/team-sharing/). To help you sort it out, here’s what you can do:
1. From the homepage, click your **profile icon** from the top corner of the page. For mobile users, tap **Menu** first to see your profile icon.
2.

Use **Revoke all access** to remove everyone’s access to your design—whether they were directly invited or inherited it through shared folders.

Use this option when:
- Your design was moved into a shared folder you don’t control.
- Unexpected people can view or edit your design.
- You want to reset all sharing and start fresh.
- You need to secure a design with sensitive content.
### How to revoke all access
Remove all shared access to your Canva design, including inherited permissions from folders, to reset sharing permissions and secure your design.
1. Open the design.
2. Go to the **Share** menu.
3. Besides the **share design,**select the **Share settings**.
4. Select **Remove access.**
5. Select whether to **Cancel**or **Yes, remove access. **
**Note:** Only editors and design owners can see and use this option.

You can save your preferred download format and options so they automatically apply to new designs of the same type on your current device.
Selecting **Save download settings** updates the default download settings for that design type on your device. These settings are stored locally and do not sync across devices.

When you select **Save download settings,** Canva saves:
- Your selected file type (for example, PNG or PDF)

4. Set the permission to Can view or Can comment.
5. Select Copy link, then send it to your external partner.
**Option 2: Invite by email**

Canva offers three AI quality tiers:

- **Ultra:** Highest quality for photos and videos. Consumes AI allowance faster and is available to paid plans only.

# Syncing audio with video
Bring your content together with music. Automatically align video cuts to the beat of a song.
We've changed how AI usage limits work in Canva. Learn more about [AI usage limits in Canva](https://www.canva.com/help/ai-access/).
### How does Beat Sync work?
Beat Sync uses AI technology to find the beats in a song. It then converts the beats into snap points on the audio track that can sync pages and other elements to the music. When "Beat Sync" is on, all pages and elements in the design will sync perfectly to the beat of your music.
### Use Beat Sync
1. Create or open an existing **video**, **presentation** or **social media design type**.
2. Add a video and an audio of your choice.
3. Select the audio pill at the bottom of the editor.
4. Select **Beat Sync** on the floating toolbar.
- **Display beat markers:** This will show in the audio pill when the audio will snap in the timeline.
- *

lect **Beat Sync** on the floating toolbar.
- **Display beat markers:** This will show in the audio pill when the audio will snap in the timeline.
- **Sync now:** This will automatically sync your audio to your elements and your pages.
For uploaded audios in your designs, make sure that you switch Beat Markers from the Beat Sync panel.
### What beat does it sync to?
Beat Sync trims the duration of the page to the first beat in the nearest bar.
### What are the limitations of Beat Sync?
- It has a 10 minutes or less in duration audio track limit.
- It is only available on Presentations, Social Media & Video doctypes.

****

Beat Sync uses AI to detect beats in your music and creates snap points on the audio track. You can use these to manually sync pages and elements to the music, or turn on Beat Sync to automatically sync everything in your design.
**What beat does it sync to?**
Beat Sync trims the duration of your page to the first beat in the nearest bar. We're working on updates that will let you sync to different beats for more editing options.
**What happens if my design content is too short?**
- If the duration is less than 1 bar, Beat Sync rounds down to the first beat of the nearest bar.

# Transform your image into a video
Use Image to Video to bring static images to life with subtle, AI-generated motion. Turn any photo or still graphic into a short, animated video clip, ideal for social posts, presentations, and product visuals.
Learn more about how this feature counts toward your [AI usage.](https://www.canva.com/help/ai-access/)
### For best results:
- Image should have: a minimum size of **256 × 224 pixels (57,344 total pixels).**
- an aspect ratio of up to **5:1 (horizontal or vertical)**.
### Transform an image into a short video using AI
1. Open your design in the Canva editor.
2. Select the image you'd like to turn into a video.
3. In the toolbar, select **Edit**.
4. Under **Tools**, select **Image to Video**.
5. Choose between **Smart** or **Custom** mode:**Smart** applies default motion automatically.
6. **Custom** allows you to describe the type of motion you want (e.g., “make the image dance”).

mode:**Smart** applies default motion automatically.
6. **Custom** allows you to describe the type of motion you want (e.g., “make the image dance”).
7. Select **Generate 5 second video** to continue. Your generated video will automatically be added to the editor.
8. Select **Generate again** to try a different result.
Note: Your final video maintains the original layout and aspect ratio of your image.
To learn more about other ways to transform your images, check out [Edit photos with Canva photo editor](https://www.canva.com/help/image-editor/)**.**
## Image to Video limitations
- Only supports 5-second video clips.
- Doesn't support premium media (e.g., stock photos).
- Doesn’t fully support face animation. For images with faces, facial motion may not render as expected.
- Images with transparent backgrounds aren’t supported.
- Some Image to Video generations may currently produce sh

## FAQs
### Is this the same as Magic Media’s video feature?
No. **Magic Media**generates videos from text prompts. **Image to Video**animates existing images with subtle motion.
### Does this feature work on all types of images?
Not all image types are supported. Image to Video doesn’t support premium media.
We’re working to support more image types, including premium images, in future updates.

Yes. If you're on the Free plan, you can use Image to Video as long as you still have monthly

Generated videos are fixed at 5 seconds. You can easily combine multiple clips or extend your design in the Canva Editor. [Learn how to create and edit videos](https://www.canva.com/help/creating-and-editing-videos/).

The video maintains your image’s original aspect ratio.

Create tables, edit data, and generate insights in Sheets using simple prompts.
This is a premium feature available with Canva Pro, Canva Teams, Canva Business, and Canva Nonprofit. It counts toward your monthly AI allowance.
This is a premium feature available with **Canva Pro, Canva Teams, Canva Business, and Canva Nonprofit**. It counts toward your monthly AI allowance. Access depends on your plan. ## What you can do with Canva AI 2.0 for Sheets
Canva AI 2.0 lets you work with data through natural language. Instead of editing cells manually, describe what you want to do, and Canva AI 2.0 can apply the change to your sheet.

- **Plans**: Canva Free, Pro, Business, Enterprise, and Nonprofits

Canva’s Content License Agreement **does not allow** you to use Free or Pro Content to design and sell your own stock content (e.g. clipart files). If you want to sell stock content, you need to create your own designs from scratch.
### Special conditions for using Canva Pro Content
There are special conditions for using Canva Pro Content in templates or products for sale. Our Content License Agreement covers this in more detail, but in general:
- If you want to create and sell templates that include Pro Content, you can only sell these as Canva template links. Read on to the templates section below to learn more about it.
- A pixel limit applies when using Pro Content in electronic publications like e-books.

## Selling templates
You can sell templates under certain conditions.
- The templates need to be an **original design**. You can use a combination of Free and Pro Content.
- You can only use **Pro Content** in template designs if they’re [shared as Canva template links](https://www.canva.com/help/share-template-link/) (e.g. a template that brings your customers back to design in Canva).
- You **can’t** sell templates with Pro Content as a PDF or other file types, whether flattened or not.
### Definition of “templates”
We define templates as a design that has a pre-determined layout and style which is intended to be **further edited** or **customized** by an end-user to produce the required final document.
This includes templates for websites, social networking websites, documents, projects, or otherwise for distribut

- **A wedding invitation is a template**because you need to fill out the details of the event in order to use it.
- **An e-book is not a template**because it’s a finished product that doesn’t require further editing by the end-user in order to use it. This applies even if the e-book has sections that an end-user can fill out. An example is a self-help book that has a section for the reader to write notes in.

### Print-on-demand service and copyright ownership
Some third-party print services may require you to agree that you **own copyright** in any design you upload to their service. If that's the case, you **can't use Canva Content** in those designs because you don't own their copyright. You only have a license to it.
If the print service only requires you to agree you have **the right** to use your design that contains Canva Content, then it’s OK to use as long as you're complying with our license terms (e.g. you aren't trying to sell Content on a standalone basis).
You’re responsible for checking the terms of third-party websites as we’re unable to advise you on these.

This is not allowed because Martina would be re-selling Content for customers to use in other applications.

### If I use Magic Edit to change certain components of a photo, can I sell the revised photo?
Only if it’s part of an original design. You can’t sell it on its own (e.g. as the only image on a t-shirt).
Manipulating a photo, whether using traditional photo-editing tools, or AI tools, is still using the underlying photo. The [Content License Agreement](https://www.canva.com/policies/content-license-agreement/) still applies to the use of that underlying photo.
We acknowledge that there might be a scenario where you’ve changed a photo so significantly with Magic Edit that it no longer resembles the original photo. However, there’s no definite rule we can provide on how much you’d need to change a photo in order for it not to be considered standalone use.

# Use Decorate in your designs
Use **Decorate** to enhance your design with AI-generated visuals. Quickly add styled elements that match your design, no manual formatting needed.
We've changed how AI access works in Canva. Learn more about [AI access in Canva](https://www.canva.com/help/ai-access/).
## How Decorate works
Decorate automatically improves the look of your design. It generates visual elements that match your existing colors, layout, and overall design, so everything stays cohesive. Results may vary depending on your page content and layout.
### Supported design types
Decorate is currently supported on most fixed-size design types (such as presentations, social media posts, posters, flyers, and standard document formats)
- It is not available in **Canva Sheets, Canva Code,**and** Canva Whiteboard**.
- Pages with extreme aspect ratios (very wide or very tall) may not support all features.

Frames let you crop images or videos into different shapes to add style and structure to your designs. Think of them as placeholders, where you can drag in your own media or choose from Canva’s library.
Use frames to highlight content, create layouts, add creative shapes, or build mockups.

# Use Layouts
Canva recommends layout options based on what’s already on your slide, so you can update your design without starting from scratch.
## What Layouts do
Applying a layout rearranges and resizes your elements to fit a professionally designed structure.
Canva suggests layouts based on what’s already on your slide, including:
- Text and images
- Graphics and photos
- Spacing
- Colors on the slide
Layouts are only available for Presentation templates.
To get layout suggestions, **unlock the elements** on your slide.
If any items are locked, you’ll see a prompt to **Unlock all elements** before continuing.
Start by [creating a design using a template](https://www.canva.com/help/use-templates/), or you can start from scratch.
### Apply a layout to your slide
For layouts to work, there should be at least one graphic, element, or text in your design.
1. Open the presentation you want to edit.
2. S

- If your page has too many elements, Layouts may not be able to provide suggestions.

# Use Magic Design to generate design templates
**Magic Design** helps you get started by suggesting templates based on your content. Whether you're creating a presentation, social post, video, or document, Magic Design analyzes the images, text, or ideas you provide and recommends layouts that match your theme and style.
You can customize these templates with:
- Your own photos, videos, and text
- Canva’s stock images, videos, and music
- AI-generated content from tools like **Magic Media** or **Canva AI Video**

# Use margins, bleed, rulers, and crop marks
Planning to print something? Turn on margins, bleed, rulers, and crop marks while designing to make sure everything prints as expected.
Margins, bleed, rulers, and crop marks aren’t available yet in Canva Docs. Changing margin, bleed, and crop mark sizes are also not available. These are fixed and are measured based on our print specifications.
We may be unable to check your design for quality control before it goes to print, so make sure you [use CMYK colors](https://www.canva.com/help/cmyk-for-print/) and [proof your designs](https://www.canva.com/help/proof-designs-print/) for print before placing your order.
## Understanding Margins in Canva
Margins are the boundary lines that help you keep important content, such as text, logos, or key visuals, safely away from the edge of your design. Turning on margins helps your layout look balanced and ensures nothing is accidentally trimmed or

visuals, safely away from the edge of your design. Turning on margins helps your layout look balanced and ensures nothing is accidentally trimmed or appears cramped when printed or exported.
It’s important to note that margins are not the same as the danger zone you’ll see in proofing. Margins act as a visual guide during design, while the danger zone marks the outer area where elements may be cut off during printing. Keeping your content within the margins helps you stay clear of the danger zone later on.
### Show margins
1. Create or open an existing design.
2. From the top menu, select **File,** then **Settings**.
3. Select **Show margins**. A border of broken lines will appear on your design pages.
4. Edit your design, and keep important elements inside the margin.
### Why margins matter
Turning on margins helps you:
- Avoid placing important text or images too close to the edge of

### Why margins matter

- Avoid placing important text or images too close to the edge of your design
- Ensure better alignment and layout for both digital and printed outputs
- Create cleaner, more professional designs
- The **Show margins** feature may not appear in some document types or older templates. Try switching to a newer Canva format or start with a blank design.
- Margins are different from the **danger zone** shown during proofing. Margins are used while designing to guide layout. The danger zone appears later, during **print preview**, and highlights areas that might be trimmed or misaligned if content is too close to the edge.

**What is Canva’s default bleed size?**

# Website DNS settings
This guide helps you connect your domain to Canva by updating DNS records. You’ll copy the records from Canva, add them to your domain host, and wait for the update to finish.
## Understand DNS basics
When we browse the internet, we use website domain names like ***canva.com***. But our browsers use Internet Protocol (IP) addresses. The Domain Name System (DNS) converts the domain names we use into IP addresses. This helps your browser locate the right website.
## Why you might need to update your website’s DNS records
Updating your domain’s DNS settings on your domain host’s website ensures **your visitors won’t get lost**.
Think of DNS as a guide to your website. When you change DNS records, browsers need time to find the new location. This update process is called DNS propagation.
## Use a subdomain
A subdomain is a part of your main domain. In the example, your domain name is the com

## Use a subdomain
A subdomain is a part of your main domain. In the example, your domain name is the complete address of your building (website). As you organize your building, you create sections or departments. In the domain world, these sections, which are still part of the main building, are called subdomains.
If you have *example.com* as your main domain for an education website, you can have *courses.example.com*as a subdomain for the subjects you offer.**By using subdomains, you create a structure for your website, making it easy for visitors to find specific information.

If there are Canva charges on your credit card or PayPal account that you don’t recognize, use our Charge Finder below.

Received an unfamiliar Canva payment? Look it up to learn what it's for.
For purchases made through App Store (iOS) or Google Play check your purchase history or refer to this [article](https://www.canva.com/help/find-read-invoices/)to help identify unfamiliar Canva charges.

## Common reasons for unrecognized charges
Here are some common reasons for charges that might not look familiar and how to manage them.
### You have more than one Canva account, Canva Teams, or Canva Business account
If you used different emails or third-party accounts (e.g. Google, Facebook), you may have multiple accounts. Check each account to see if the charge is for any of them. Teams have separate billing. If you don't see the charge in your invoices, it might be for another team. Found the account but don’t remember your password? [Reset your password](https://www.canva.com/login/reset).
### Your free trial ended
Canva plans renew automatically. If you don't cancel before your trial ends, you'll be charged for the renewal.
To cancel your plan, see [Cancel a Canva plan](https://www.canva.com/help/cancel-canva-plan/).

### Your charge shows up earlier than expected
Canva fees follow GMT time. We also charge you a day before your billing date. So if you’re on a monthly plan and your billing date is on the 31st, you’ll be charged on the 30th (and on the 28th in February).
### You were charged a credit card authentication
A credit card authentication charge (sometimes called pre-authorization) is a small temporary charge, usually around $1 or the local currency equivalent, that appears when you add or update your card. It isn’t an actual payment — it’s placed by our payment processor and your bank to verify that the card is valid

# Write better prompts to maximize your AI allowance
All premium AI tools share a single monthly allowance. Some tools, like image and video generation, use more allowance than simpler ones like [Background Generator](https://www.canva.com/help/bg-generator/) and[Magic Formulas](https://www.canva.com/help/use-magic-formulas/). To get the most out of your allowance, write clear prompts to minimize the need to re-generate results.
The most important thing is to be as clear and descriptive as possible with your prompts, right from the start.
## Get better results with conversational design in Canva AI 2.0
**Canva AI 2.0 is available with Canva Pro, Canva Teams, Canva Business, and Canva Nonprofit.**
Canva AI 2.0 works as a conversational design partner that can take multiple editing and design actions autonomously when prompted. Because of this, it uses more AI power than single-prompt features and consumes your shared AI allowance based on:

- **Designs referenced:**When you include designs in a task, larger files use more AI allowance. For example, a 40-slide presentation will use more than a 5-slide presentation.
- **Task complexity:**More complex tasks require more steps, which increases AI allowance usage.
- **Tools used:**Tasks that use multiple AI tools consume more allowance than those that use fewer tools.
- **Models used:**More complex tasks or higher quality outputs may use more advanced AI models, than simpler tasks. The more powerful the AI tool, the more AI allowance used.
